Babylon's Processional Way gleams with glazed blue tiles as priests lead white bulls toward Marduk's ziggurat, incense smoke drifting over date-palm gardens.
Teotihuacan's Avenue of the Dead swarms with pilgrims bearing obsidian blades, turquoise mosaics glinting on temple facades above packed plaza stalls.
Chang'an's eastern market roars with silk merchants, bronze mirrors, and caged songbirds while Tang officials in robes negotiate beside lacquered palanquins.
Angkor's canal network teems with dugout canoes loaded with rice, clay pots, and fish as sandstone baray reservoirs reflect towering temple spires.
Thebes' harbor bustles with Syrian traders unloading cedar logs and amphorae while painted tomb-workers haggle over linen beneath acacia-shaded beer stalls.
Ctesiphon's vaulted bazaar echoes with Sassanian armorers hammering steel, saffron dealers, and Sogdian caravans watering camels beside the Tigris wharves.
Aksum's granite obelisk plaza fills with incense merchants, ivory traders, and Ge'ez scribes recording tributes on parchment beneath carved stone thrones.
Mycenae's cyclopean gates admit olive-oil amphorae on ox-carts while bronze-workers forge Linear B tablets near the megaron's frescoed lion guardians.
Mohenjo-daro's grid streets show brick workshops with terracotta drains, bead-makers threading carnelian, and granary workers measuring barley beside the great bath.
Tiwanaku's sunken courtyards host llama caravans delivering quinoa and potatoes as stonemasons carve monoliths near reed-boat docks on Lake Titicaca's shore.
Birka's wooden jetties swarm with Norse knarrs unloading amber and furs while smiths forge iron rivets beside longhouses thatched with Baltic reeds.
Rapa Nui's Orongo village shows stone-slab houses clustered near crater lakes, canoe-builders shaping totora reeds, and moai-carvers descending Rano Raraku's quarry.
Uruk's ziggurat district swarms with reed-basket porters hauling dates and barley while temple accountants press cylinder seals into wet clay beneath striped awnings.
Tikal's plastered plaza fills with Maya merchants trading cacao beans and jade celts as howler monkeys screech above red-painted stucco temple pyramids.
Luoyang's bronze foundries belch smoke as Zhou artisans cast ritual vessels while ox-carts deliver millet through rammed-earth walls guarded by halberd sentries.
Pagan's riverside docks bustle with teak barges unloading lacquerware and betel nut as Pyu monks in saffron robes bless gilded stupa foundations.
Persepolis' Apadana stairways stream with tribute-bearers carrying Bactrian gold and lapis while Persian guards in scaled armor flank carved stone reliefs.
Knossos' west magazines store oil pithoi tall as men while frescoed corridors echo with scribes tallying Linear A tablets beside saffron-dyed wool bundles.
Kerma's mud-brick defenses tower above Nubian potters shaping black-topped vessels as cattle herds raise dust clouds near whitewashed temple compounds with mica inlay.
Copán's ball court fills with spectators as Maya nobles in quetzal plumes watch rubber-ball players beneath hieroglyphic stairways recording dynastic conquest dates.
Nara's Heijō palace grounds show vermilion pillars and tile-roofed halls where courtiers in silk kimonos pass lacquered ox-carts carrying tribute rice bales.
Tyre's island harbor swarms with Phoenician galleys loading murex-dyed purple cloth and cedar planks while glassblowers shape translucent vessels near limestone quays.
Dún Ailinne's timber palisades encircle Celtic roundhouses with conical thatch as bronze-smiths hammer La Tène spiral-patterned shields beside cattle-pen enclosures.
Raiatea's coral-stone marae platforms host Polynesian chiefs exchanging tapa cloth and pearl-shell fishhooks as outrigger canoes beach on black volcanic sand.
Caral's sunken plaza amphitheater hosts musicians with bone flutes and conch trumpets while laborers haul reed shicra bags of stone up stepped pyramid terraces.
